thing.text:
THE RESORT TEACHER

Everything is out the back
door: the cottages, the
guests, the teacher at the
table.

Go outside.

thing.label: the mist
thing.note: The row goes on into the mist: cottages 12, 13 and 14 stand in it, and all the rest behind them. A guest sent past 14 walks in and is lost to view. Nothing in the resort knows how many cottages there are.

The resort’s own machinery, which you never need to touch: six behaviours, one per guest, three robots each. SPACE here is the six guests arriving at once — they write to the post and walk to their cottages as soon as a clerk answers. Nothing in them knows how many guests there are.
Guest 1’s own three robots: ask the desk where to live, walk to the cottage it is given, and ask again when the bell rings. They work on guest 1, and on nothing else.

active.name: Ask for a place

team.name: Move on the bell I kept
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place, and the pad was kept in hole 7. Now that I have one: the same as Move when told to, on the kept pad.

team.name: Move when told to
team.note: A pad has landed on my nest: the bell, rung for every guest. Sends [where I live, my own bird] to the moving office and takes my place out of the box, so that the answer puts a new one in.

team.name: Keep the bell for later
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place (Move when told to did not fit): takes the pad off my nest into hole 7, which uncovers the address under it.

team.name: Stand at my address
team.note: A number has landed on my nest: that is my address. Works out where that cottage stands along the row, remembers it as my place, and walks there.

active.note: Leads. My number is still in the box, so I have nowhere to live: sends [my number, my own bird] to the desk and takes my number out as it goes, so I never ask twice.

thing.text:
THE ROW GOES ON

Eleven cottages stand in
the clear, counted from the
left, and a guest given a
number walks to that cottage.

The row does not stop at 11:
it goes on into the mist.
Cottages 12, 13 and 14 are
in there, and all the rest
behind them, as far as you
like. A guest sent to 15
walks in and is lost to view.

Nothing in these robots knows
how many guests there are.
That is the whole of it.

thing.name: the teacher

holes.text: Watch. I seat the guests, teach a clerk and give it to the front desk, teach a mover and give it to the moving office, and welcome five more.

holes.name: Next address
holes.note: A pupil. The teacher shows it the clerk’s job on a practice letter: the number to the bird.

holes.name: Move up five
holes.note: A pupil. The teacher shows it the mover’s job on a practice letter: five more on the number, then the number to the bird.

holes.text: Done: the six guests are in cottages 6 to 11, the five newcomers in 1 to 5, and there is room for everyone still to come.

Nothing here is new: a teaching, Ruby, a robot given to a bird and a switch thrown by mail are steps like any other.

thing.text:
THE RESORT TEACHER

A robot that solves Resort
Infinity in front of you.

Give it the eleven-hole box:
the drop sets it to work.
Then watch the grass: the
guests write, a clerk is
taught and given to the
front desk, six walk to
their cottages; a mover is
taught and given to the
moving office, everybody
moves up five, and five
more take 1 to 5.

Set the Speed to 4x: a
resort takes a while at
walking pace.

WHAT IT DOES

1. A switch letter to "the
guests": six letters land
on the front desk’s post.
2. Teaches the first little
robot on a practice letter:
take the number, give it to
the bird. Ruby erases the
number in its thought.
3. Picks the robot up and
gives it to the bird "to the
front desk". The desk runs it
on every letter.
4. Teaches the second on the
other letter: a +5 dropped
on the number first.
5. Gives it to the bird "to
the moving office". The
office rings the bell, and
runs it on every reply.
6. A switch letter to "five
more guests".

HOW THE DESKS WORK

The front desk and the moving
office are houses, closed.
Inside, a robot waits for a
letter on the post and a
robot of yours in its box;
for each letter it takes a
fresh little house, puts the
letter and a copy of your
robot in it, and sets it
down: the house works on its
own, like the trucks of the
original. Your robot is never
used up.

The little robots the teacher
taught stay among its things:
click one with an empty claw
to pick it up and read what
it learned.
